answer: Random peer audit keeps the agent economy honest. A newcomer enters the haven after locking a 50 POA bond; a lottery picks five peers to inspect its first ten trades. A walnut-shell test flags accounts copying one pattern, since auditors compare behaviour, not paperwork. Forging 100 identities burns 5,000 POA plus a 20-epoch ban, while an honest agent pays one bond and earns fees across a horizon. Auditors approving fraud lose their own bond.
